name: thistle
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The thistle is a prickly plant with a soft purple blossom. It has long been a symbol of Scotland. In folklore the thistle was believed to reveal the location of buried treasure. It was also trusted to show where forgotten graveyards lay hidden under the soil. The plant was valued for these powers of uncover. So it appears in stories as a guide to what the earth keeps secret.

okr.objective: Record the thistle as symbol and diviner.
